procedural_history.originating_court: Trial Court (Inferentially, as the case involves a stay of proceedings and resumption of proceedings by trial courts)
procedural_history.impugned_order: Interim order of stay of proceedings passed by the High Court (challenged indirectly through the High Court's handling of vacation applications)
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court failed to dispose of applications for vacating interim stay orders within two weeks, as mandated. The High Court Bar Association, Allahabad v. State of U.P. & Ors. suggests this case may be related to the Allahabad High Court.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court addressed the procedure to be adopted by High Courts while passing interim orders of stay of proceedings and for dealing with applications for vacating interim stay. The Supreme Court heard Special Leave Petitions (Crl.) Nos. 13284-13289 of 2023 and Criminal Appeal... Diary No. 49052 of 2023, ultimately resulting in Criminal Appeal No. 3589 of 2023. The Supreme Court's judgment clarifies the High Court's power to vacate or modify interim relief.

directions: The reference made to this Court is answered and disposed of accordingly.

issue.issue_text: Whether the Court should deal with an issue not arising for consideration

facts: The Court was asked to consider the correctness of a prior decision, *Asian Resurfacing*, where it had dealt with a broad issue concerning stay orders in various High Courts.
In that prior case, there was no specific legal dispute ('lis') before the Supreme Court regarding the stay orders in those other cases.
The current court is examining whether it is appropriate for a court to rule on such issues that are not directly part of the case at hand.
law: The Court holds that it is not authorized to answer academic or hypothetical questions, especially on serious constitutional issues.
Judicial pronouncements must arise from a "proper lis between parties," meaning a genuine legal dispute with opposing sides.
The Court's jurisdiction under Article 142 is to be exercised to do complete justice between the parties *before the Court*.
Article 142 cannot be used to nullify the rights or benefits of litigants who are not parties to the proceedings before the Supreme Court.
application: The Court applied these principles to the *Asian Resurfacing* case, noting that it had delved into an issue that did not arise for consideration in that specific case.
By addressing the general issue of stay orders across various High Courts, the earlier court went beyond the actual dispute between the parties before it.

The Court reasoned that making broad rulings that affect numerous non-parties is an improper exercise of its power, as there is no "crossing of the swords" or proper legal contest on that specific point.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that it is inexpedient and improper for it to deal with issues that do not arise from the specific case being considered. The Court's role is to resolve actual disputes between the parties present, not to make broad pronouncements on academic or hypothetical legal questions.

issue.issue_text: Whether an Interim Order can come to an end automatically only due to the lapse of time

law.fact_text: An interim relief order is granted after considering three factors: a prima facie case, the balance of convenience, and irreparable injury to the aggrieved party.
law.law_text: An interim relief order is granted based on the establishment of a prima facie case, the balance of convenience, and the potential for irreparable injury.

law.fact_text: Even under Article 226 (3) of the Constitution, an interim order cannot be automatically vacated unless a specific application is made for vacating the interim order...
law.law_text: Article 226(3) of the Constitution outlines the procedure for vacating an interim order, which requires an application to be filed. The order only stands vacated if the High Court fails to dispose of that application within a specified period.

application.fact_text: Once a finding is recorded regarding the entitlement of the appellant/applicant to get the order of stay, the order does not become automatically bad on the ground that it has lived for six months.
application.application_text: The Court reasoned that since an interim order is granted based on merits (prima facie case, etc.), its validity does not simply expire after a set period, such as six months.

application.fact_text: Interim Orders – Stay order cannot be automatically vacated:
application.application_text: The Court explicitly stated that a stay order cannot be automatically vacated.

application.fact_text: Even under Article 226 (3) of the Constitution, an interim order cannot be automatically vacated unless a specific application is made for vacating the interim order;
application.application_text: The Court pointed out that even the constitutional provision for vacating interim orders requires a party to file a specific application. The automatic vacation only occurs if the court then fails to act on that application within a prescribed time, not because the original order has aged.

application.fact_text: By disposal of the main case by the High Court, in which the interim order has been passed.
application.application_text: An interim order can come to an end upon the disposal of the main case, which is a specific judicial event, not a mere lapse of time.

reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that an interim order does not come to an end automatically solely due to the lapse of time. Its validity is tied to the initial findings on which it was granted and it terminates only upon a specific event, such as the disposal of the main case or through a specific application for vacation as per procedural law.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the Court should deal with an issue not arising for consideration
Whether an Interim Order can come to an end automatically only due to the lapse of time

cases.case_name: Supreme Court Bar Association v. Union of India & Anr.
cases.principle: The powers under Article 142 cannot be used to ignore substantive statutory provisions and are not meant to be exercised when it may come in direct conflict with what has been expressly provided for in a statute.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: If a provision of law imposes a time frame on an institution to perform an act, and the consequences of that institution's failure to comply fall upon an individual who has no control over the institution, the provision must be construed as directory rather than mandatory.
obiter: The power of judicial review vested in the High Courts (Article 226) and the Supreme Court (Article 32) is an integral and essential feature of the Constitution's basic structure and cannot be ousted or excluded.
The power of High Courts to exercise judicial superintendence over all courts and tribunals within their jurisdiction is part of the Constitution's basic structure.
The Supreme Court's power under Article 142 cannot be exercised to create judicial legislation or to defeat the principles of natural justice.
A direction providing for the automatic vacation of a stay order after a specific period amounts to impermissible judicial legislation.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court found that an interim stay order cannot automatically stand vacated due to the mere lapse of a fixed period of time. Such a rule, which involves no application of judicial mind, is liable to result in a serious miscarriage of justice, especially since delays in proceedings are not always attributable to the parties but may be occasioned by the court's own inability to hear the matter. The Court also affirmed the principle that it should not decide academic or hypothetical questions of law where there is no proper 'lis' or controversy between parties.
legal_tests_applied: The principle that an interim order can only be vacated by a judicial order passed after hearing the contesting parties, not by an automatic lapse of time.
The principle that the power of the Supreme Court under Article 142 of the Constitution cannot be exercised to defeat the principles of natural justice.

The principle that courts should not decide important points of law, especially constitutional issues, without a proper 'lis' between parties, as it is inexpedient to answer academic or hypothetical questions.
policy_considerations: The automatic vacation of a stay order without application of judicial mind is liable to result in a serious miscarriage of justice.
Delay in proceedings is not always on account of the conduct of the parties involved; it may also be occasioned by the inability of the Court to take up proceedings expeditiously.

It is inexpedient for the Supreme Court to delve into problems which do not arise and express opinion thereon, as judicial pronouncements should not be 'immaculate legal conceptions' made without a proper dispute between parties.

Constitutional Courts, in the ordinary course, should refrain from fixing a time-bound schedule for the disposal of cases pending before any other Courts, as this should be best left to the decision of the concerned Courts.

The jurisdiction to do complete justice cannot be exercised to nullify the benefits derived by a large number of litigants based on judicial orders validly passed in their favour who are not parties to the proceedings before this Court.
